note: Evaluation corpus for the notebook overview map. Real notebooks are referenced, not vendored: fetch.py pulls each one at a pinned commit into .cache/, which is gitignored. That keeps third-party licensing out of this repo and keeps the corpus reproducible — a pinned sha is the same bytes forever, a branch name is not.

remote.why: Real end-to-end ML project, 243 cells. Headings exist but nowhere near one per section, so the segmenter has to do actual work between them.
The heading-rich control: 286 cells, 142 of them markdown. If the deterministic pass ever looks good, it should look good here — and that is the point of having it in the set.
Real course EDA, 54 cells with only 6 headings. Heading-poor and mid-sized.
Personal-project EDA, 87 cells. The most common shape on GitHub and the one the panel will actually meet.
Small end of the range, 21 cells. Guards against a segmenter that only behaves on long inputs.

local.why: The existing hard probe: 57 cells, one markdown cell, no defs, out-of-order execution.
The existing non-ML probe — a parameter sweep rather than a data pipeline.

Synthetic, deliberately nasty: 154 cells, 3 markdown cells, copy-paste-tweak runs, abandoned attempts interleaved rather than grouped, a topic resumed 40 cells later, re-runs and never-run cells scattered mid-file.

Synthetic control, and a cautionary tale: 122 cells written as 19 tidy phases each under its own markdown heading. Written by hand while demoing the panel, and the map looked excellent — because segment() puts a boundary on every heading, so the notebook had already been segmented by its author. Kept in the corpus precisely so that flattery is visible as a number next to the others.
